## Appearance

Marilla Cuthbert is a tall, thin, gaunt woman with sharp angles and no curves. She has dark hair streaked with gray that she wears twisted into a hard little knot at the back of her head, held in place with two wire hairpins. Over time, her hair has grown grayer, and her appearance reflects a tired look, complete with wrinkled cheeks and hard, work-worn hands.

## Personality

A self-contained and determined woman, Marilla Cuthbert possesses a sensible, pragmatic outlook and views the world purely through prose. She is characterized by a narrow experience and a rigid conscience, detesting stinginess in children while scorning poetic weakness. Although she maintains a neat, order-loving household, her uncomfortable ignorance can occasionally make her crisp, curt, and somewhat sarcastic, particularly when suffering from headaches. By nature and habit, she remains stoic and reserved in expressing her affection, finding it difficult to put her deep feelings into words. Additionally, she is celebrated locally for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine, and she motivated herself to keep a pair of twins despite concerns over whether she could afford to do so.

## History

When Marilla Cuthbert sent [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) to the train station to fetch an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), he returned instead with a young girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), shocking Marilla. Though initially determined to return the child, Marilla felt deep pity upon hearing Anne's difficult past, refused to pass her to a harsh neighbor, and agreed to adopt her, resolving to educate her properly. She raised [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) with a mixture of stern discipline and affection, managing her outbursts, eccentric prayers, and various mishaps, such as when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) dyed her hair green or accidentally served currant wine to her friend [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md). Though often exasperated by Anne's antics, Marilla grew deeply fond of her and felt profound pride in the girl's achievements as she excelled in school. When [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) tragically died of heart failure and an oculist warned Marilla that her failing eyesight meant giving up reading and sewing, she considered selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). However, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) gave up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla, and teach locally. Marilla later agreed to temporarily foster two orphaned twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md), whose uncle subsequently passed away and left a trust fund that allowed them to stay permanently at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Despite the chaotic challenges of raising the mischievous [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) alongside [Dora](../character/dora.md), Marilla found herself growing attached to the boy. When her long-time neighbor [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) lost her husband, Marilla invited Mrs. [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), a living arrangement that freed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to leave and pursue her dream of attending [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college).

## Quotes

> "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P29](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0029)

> "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)

> "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself. You’d likely set the place on fire."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P44](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0044)

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P11](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0011)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla serves as Anne's adoptive guardian and parent. Initially intending to adopt a boy to help on the farm, Marilla is persuaded to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) after learning of her difficult past as an orphan and deciding to raise and educate her properly. Though frequently put off by Anne's dramatic chatter and daydreaming, Marilla takes her upbringing seriously and comes to comfort her during times of shared grief.

- Parent of — adoptive parent / guardian raising her  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089), [v1 CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit P3](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P32](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0032), +1 more</sub>

### [Martin](../character/martin.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--martin.md)

[Martin](../character/martin.md) works at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) under Marilla's authority, driving for her and handling farm duties. Following Matthew's death, he assists with the day-to-day operations around the household and farm property.

- Commands — drives for her and works at Green Gables  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P2](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P28](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0028), [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P29](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0029)</sub>

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) is Marilla's outspoken neighbor and friend. The two frequently consult each other on local news and personal advice, though Rachel's blunt demeanor occasionally causes tension, such as when her harsh insults toward [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) force Marilla to mediate an apology. Despite occasional disagreements, they remain close companions who visit regularly and travel together.

- Comrade of — traveling together to a political mass meeting in Charlottetown  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001)</sub>
